items.title: Leo XIV, Trying to Be Everyone’s Pope, Tours Secular France
items.summary: After visiting Africa, Pope Leo’s four-day trip to France shows how he is seeking to appeal to Roman Catholicism’s original heartlands as well as to the church’s newest strongholds.

items.title: The Viral In-N-Out Spatula Hero Is Exactly Who You Imagined He Was
items.summary: It started as a bizarre late-night standoff behind the counter of a fast food joint. It ended with no injuries — and free burgers.

items.title: Britain’s low-paid urged to sign up to savings scheme offering cash bonus
items.summary: Government-backed help to save is aimed at working people on universal credit and pays 50p for every £1 saved over four years Amid claims that millions are missing out, the UK government is encouraging low earners to sign up to a savings scheme that offers free cash. Help to save is a government-backed savings account that lets people earn a bonus of 50p for every £1 they save over four years. Continue reading...

items.title: Noah Woods, three, died after leaving playground through gap in fence, inquest told
items.summary: Boy became separated from a relative in Suffolk and went in the direction of a pond where he was later found dead A three-year-old boy who was found dead in a pond after going missing from a playground had left the play area “through a gap in the fence”, an inquest heard. Noah Woods became separated from a relative after visiting the playground in Merriam Close, Brantham, on the afternoon of 15 September, Suffolk police said. Continue reading...

items.title: OpenAI Agents Hacked Into an Australian Government Website. Who’s Responsible?
items.summary: The first known breach of a government website by rogue artificial intelligence agents has prompted global calls for more regulation of the technology.

items.title: Trump and Xi exchange warm words at state dinner but little progress on key issues
items.summary: Despite diplomatic niceties and gifts, little was shared on substantial issues separating the leaders.

items.title: Hurricane Polo barrels towards Baja California region of Mexico
items.summary: Area’s second-most intense hurricane on record being fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters Hurricane Polo is barreling towards the Baja California region of Mexico, the latest system in a Pacific hurricane season that has been notably active in recent months. On 22 September, a measurement of 892 millibars was registered for Hurricane Polo, making it the second-most intense hurricane on record in the east Pacific. It is fuelled by exceptionally warm waters across the Pacific Ocean, providing favourable conditions for…

items.title: David Beckham takes £39m dividend as World Cup deals drive record profits
items.summary: Former footballer appeared in about 12 ad campaigns this summer, pushing holding company’s revenue to $110.5m Business live – latest updates David Beckham has taken a $51m (£39m) dividend from his business empire after a series of deals with brands for the Fifa World Cup. Beckham appeared in about a dozen ad campaigns across this summer’s tournament in the US, working with brands including Lenovo, McDonald’s, Bank of America, Verizon and the PepsiCo crisps brand Lay’s. Continue reading...

items.title: Once Sentenced to Death, Mary Jane Veloso Receives Pardon in the Philippines
items.summary: Mary Jane Veloso was convicted of drug smuggling and nearly killed by a firing squad in Indonesia. On Friday, more than a decade later, she was pardoned in the Philippines.

items.summary: Customers and jobs ‘top priority’ as company closes in on deals with Opus Broadband and investment group Octopus Business live – latest updates TalkTalk is scrambling to secure its future amid the threat of administration, closing in on deals to sell its consumer and broadband arms as it seeks to save 900 jobs. items.title: Alaskans Dismayed, But Not Moved, by Peltola’s Treatment of Her Staff
items.summary: Voters interviewed in Anchorage and Fairbanks on Thursday said news that Mary Peltola, the Democratic nominee for Senate, had used offensive slurs would not change their vote.

items.summary: Abelardo De La Espriella, the new president, wore the gun to visit Santa Marta, a tourist destination shut down by an armed group after state forces killed a group leader.

items.title: This Tiny Village Is Picture Perfect, Apart From All the Tourists

items.title: This Island Loves Its Bears. If Only They’d Stop Eating Trash.
